title: Bands named for places; the camps and Japanese Tea Garden
summary: Henderson explains bands took the name of the venue (Alamo, Cinderella etc.), and the group tries to name camps out at Little Woods and Milneburg.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. I forgot about the jizznit dances. Whose band was that? That was Talbert.

He was at the head of the band at that particular time.

blocks.s: Mrs. George Henderson (wife of George Henderson)
blocks.x: That was his band. They were sharp, they used the jutsedas and everything. They had suits glowing.

They were just named the band after the place. Like when we were playing at the Levita, it was the Levita band. We were playing at the Foyne, it was the Foyne band. We played at the Alamo, it was the Alamo band. We played at the Alamo and the Levita. Where was the Alamo? The Alamo was on Canal in... Dauphine, Nethanale. Right where Grant is. Yeah, where Grant's now. Then you played at the Lake too.

blocks.s: Mrs. George Henderson (wife of George Henderson)
blocks.x: Was it Jitney? Yeah, Jitney played the South. Then you played at the Lake of Water.
